text: Let the point $P(α,β)$ be at a unit distance from each of the two lines $L_{1}:3x-4y+12=0$, and $L_{2}:8x+6y+11=0$. If $P$ lies below $L_{1}$ and above $L_{2}$, then $100(α+β)$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
$P$ below $L_{1}$ means $β<\dfrac{3α+12}{4}$, i.e. $3α-4β+12>0$; $P$ above $L_{2}$ means $β>-\dfrac{8α+11}{6}$, i.e. $8α+6β+11>0$.

Unit distance from $L_{1}$: $\dfrac{3α-4β+12}{5}=1\Rightarrow 3α-4β=-7$.

Unit distance from $L_{2}$: $\dfrac{8α+6β+11}{10}=1\Rightarrow 8α+6β=-1$.

Adding $3\times$ the first and $2\times$ the second: $9α-12β+16α+12β=-21-2\Rightarrow α=-\dfrac{23}{25}$, and then $β=\dfrac{3α+7}{4}=\dfrac{53}{50}$.

$100(α+β)=100\left (-\dfrac{46}{50}+\dfrac{53}{50}\right )=14$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text: Let the foci of the ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{16}+\frac{y^{2}}{7}=1$ and the hyperbola $\frac{x^{2}}{144}-\frac{y^{2}}{α}=\frac{1}{25}$ coincide. Then the length of the latus rectum of the hyperbola is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Ellipse : $\frac{x^{2}}{16}+\frac{y^{2}}{7}=1$

Eccentricity $=\sqrt{1-\frac{7}{16}}=\frac{3}{4}$

Foci $\equiv (\pm ae,0)\equiv (\pm 3,0)$

Hyperbola : $\frac{x^{2}}{\left (\frac{144}{25}\right )}-\frac{y^{2}}{\left (\frac{α}{25}\right )}=1$

Eccentricity $=\sqrt{1+\frac{α}{144}}=\frac{1}{12}\sqrt{144+α}$

Foci $\equiv (\pm ae,0)\equiv \left (\pm \frac{12}{5}\qquad .\frac{1}{12}\sqrt{144+α},0\right )$

If foci coincide then $3=\frac{1}{5}\sqrt{144+α}\Rightarrow α=81$

Hence, hyperbola is $\frac{x^{2}}{\left (\frac{12}{5}\right )^{2}}-\frac{y^{2}}{\left (\frac{9}{5}\right )^{2}}=1$

Length of latus rectum $=2.\qquad \frac{\frac{81}{25}}{\frac{12}{5}}=\frac{27}{10}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text: Let $⃗{a}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$ and let $⃗{b}$ be a vector such that $⃗{a}\times ⃗{b}=2\hat{i}-\hat{k}$ and $⃗{a}\cdot ⃗{b}=3$. Then the projection of $⃗{b}$ on the vector $⃗{a}-⃗{b}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\vec{a}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\widehat{k}$

$\vec{a}\times \vec{b}=2\hat{i}-\widehat{k}$

$\vec{a}\quad .\vec{b}=3$

$|\vec{a}\times \vec{b}|^{2}+|\vec{a}.\vec{b}|^{2}=|\vec{a}|^{2}.|\vec{b}|^{2}$

$\Rightarrow 5+9=6|\vec{b}|^{2}$

$\Rightarrow |b|^{2}=\frac{7}{3}$

$|\vec{a}-\vec{b}|=\sqrt{|\vec{a}|^{2}+|\vec{b}|^{2}-2\vec{a}.\vec{b}}=\sqrt{\frac{7}{3}}$

projection of $\vec{b}$ on $\vec{a}-\vec{b}=\frac{\vec{b}.(\vec{a}-\vec{b})}{|\vec{a}-\vec{b}|}$

$=\frac{\vec{b}.\vec{a}-|\vec{b}|^{2}}{|\vec{a}-\vec{b}|}=\frac{3-\frac{7}{3}}{\sqrt{\frac{7}{3}}}$

$=\frac{2}{\sqrt{21}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text: $2\sin \left (\frac{π}{22}\right )\sin \left (\frac{3π}{22}\right )\sin \left (\frac{5π}{22}\right )\sin \left (\frac{7π}{22}\right )\sin \left (\frac{9π}{22}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $θ=\dfrac{π}{11}$, so $11θ=π$. Using $\sin \left (\dfrac{π}{2}-t\right )=\cos t$:

$\sin \dfrac{π}{22}=\cos 5θ,\sin \dfrac{3π}{22}=\cos 4θ,\sin \dfrac{5π}{22}=\cos 3θ,\sin \dfrac{7π}{22}=\cos 2θ,\sin \dfrac{9π}{22}=\cos θ$

So the expression is $P=2\cos θ\cos 2θ\cos 3θ\cos 4θ\cos 5θ$.

Since $3θ=π-8θ$, $\cos 3θ=-\cos 8θ$; since $5θ=π-6θ$ and $16θ=2π-6θ$, $\cos 5θ=-\cos 6θ=-\cos 16θ$. Hence $\cos 3θ\cos 5θ=\cos 8θ\cos 16θ$ and

$P=2\cos θ\cos 2θ\cos 4θ\cos 8θ\cos 16θ$

Multiplying and dividing by $\sin θ$ and applying $2\sin A\cos A=\sin 2A$ five times:

$\cos θ\cos 2θ\cos 4θ\cos 8θ\cos 16θ=\dfrac{\sin 32θ}{2^{5}\sin θ}$

As $32θ=2π+\dfrac{10π}{11}$, $\sin 32θ=\sin \dfrac{10π}{11}=\sin \dfrac{π}{11}=\sin θ$, so the product of cosines is $\dfrac{1}{32}$.

$P=2\times \dfrac{1}{32}=\dfrac{1}{16}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text: Let $A=\{1,2,3,4,5,6,7\}$. Define $B=\{T\subseteq A$ : either $1\notin T$ or $2\in T\}$ and $C=\{T\subseteq A:$ the sum of all the elements of $T$ is a prime number $\}$. Then the number of elements in the set $B\cup C$ is $________________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\because$ $(B\cup C)^{'}=B^{'}\cap C^{'}$

B' is a set containing sub sets of A containing element 1 and not containing 2.

And C' is a set containing subsets of A whose sum of elements is not prime.

So, we need to calculate number of subsets of {3, 4, 5, 6, 7} whose sum of elements plus 1 is composite.

Number of such 5 elements subset = 1

Number of such 4 elements subset = 3 (except selecting 3 or 7)

Number of such 3 elements subset = 6 (except selecting {3, 4, 5}, {3, 6, 7}, {4, 5, 7} or {5, 6, 7})

Number of such 2 elements subset = 7 (except selecting {3, 7}, {4, 6}, {5, 7})

Number of such 1 elements subset = 3 (except selecting {4} or {6})

Number of such 0 elements subset = 1

$n(B^{'}\qquad \cap C^{'})=21\Rightarrow n(B\cup C)=2^{7}-21=107$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text: Let $f(x)$ be a quadratic polynomial with leading coefficient 1 such that $f(0)=p,p\neq 0$, and $f(1)=\frac{1}{3}$. If the equations $f(x)=0$ and $f\circ f\circ f\circ f(x)=0$ have a common real root, then $f(-3)$ is equal to $________________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $f(x)=(x-α)(x-β)$

It is given that $f(0)=p\Rightarrow αβ=p$

and $f(1)=\frac{1}{3}\Rightarrow (1-α)(1-β)=\frac{1}{3}$

Now, let us assume that, $α$ is the common root of $f(x)=0$ and $fofofof(x)=0$

$fofofof(x)=0$

$\Rightarrow fofof(0)=0$

$\Rightarrow fof(p)=0$

So, $f(p)$ is either $α$ or $β$.

$(p-α)(p-β)=α$

$(αβ-α)(αβ-β)=α\Rightarrow (β-1)(α-1)β=1$ ($\because$ $α\neq 0$)

So, $β=3$

$(1-α)(1-3)=\frac{1}{3}$

$α=\frac{7}{6}$

$f(x)=\left (x-\frac{7}{6}\right )(x-3)$

$f(-3)=\left (-3-\frac{7}{6}\right )(3-3)=25$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text:
Let $A=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & a & a \\ 0 & 1 & b \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ],a,b\in \mathrm{ℝ}$. If for some 

$n\in \mathrm{ℕ},A^{n}=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 48 & 2160 \\ 0 & 1 & 96 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]$ then $n+a+b$ is equal to $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Write $A=I+B$, where

$B=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 0 & a & a \\ 0 & 0 & b \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right ],B^{2}=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 0 & 0 & ab \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array}\right ],B^{3}=O$

Since $I$ and $B$ commute, the binomial expansion of $(I+B)^{n}$ stops after the $B^{2}$ term:

$A^{n}=I+nB+\dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}B^{2}=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & na & na+\dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}ab \\ 0 & 1 & nb \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]$

Comparing with the given matrix: $na=48$, $nb=96$ and $na+\dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}ab=2160$.

With $a=\dfrac{48}{n}$ and $b=\dfrac{96}{n}$, so that $ab=\dfrac{4608}{n^{2}}$, the last equation becomes

$48+\dfrac{2304(n-1)}{n}=2160\Rightarrow 2304(n-1)=2112n\Rightarrow 192n=2304\Rightarrow n=12$

Then $a=\dfrac{48}{12}=4$ and $b=\dfrac{96}{12}=8$, so $n+a+b=12+4+8=24$.

Hence, the answer is 24.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text: The sum of the maximum and minimum values of the function $f(x)=|5x-7|+\left [x^{2}+2x\right ]$ in the interval $\left [\frac{5}{4},2\right ]$, where $[t]$ is the greatest integer $\leq t$, is $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=|5x-7|+[x^{2}+2x]$

$=|5x-7|+[(x+1)^{2}]-1$

Critical points of

$f(x)=\frac{7}{5},\sqrt{5}-1,\sqrt{6}-1,\sqrt{7}-1,\sqrt{8}-1,2$

$\therefore$ Maximum or minimum value of $f(x)$ occur at critical points or boundary points

$\therefore$ $f\left (\frac{5}{4}\right )=\frac{3}{4}+4=\frac{19}{4}$

$f\left (\frac{7}{5}\right )=0+4=4$

as both $|5x-7|$ and $x^{2}+2x$ are increasing in nature after $x=\frac{7}{5}$

$\therefore$ $f(2)=3+8=11$

$\therefore$ $f\left (\frac{7}{5}\right )_{\min }=4$ and $f(2)_{\max }=11$

Sum is $4+11=15$

text:
Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation

$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{4y^{3}+2yx^{2}}{3xy^{2}+x^{3}},y(1)=1$.

If for some $n\in \mathrm{ℕ},y(2)\in [n-1,n)$, then $n$ is equal to $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y}{x}\frac{(4y^{2}+2x^{2})}{(3y^{2}+x^{2})}$

Put $y=vx$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}=v+x\frac{dv}{dx}$

$\Rightarrow v+x\frac{dv}{dx}=\frac{v(4v^{2}+2)}{(3v^{2}+1)}$

$\Rightarrow x\frac{dv}{dx}=v\left (\frac{(4v^{2}+2-3v^{2}-1)}{3v^{2}+1}\right )$

$\Rightarrow \int (3v^{2}+1)\frac{dv}{v^{3}+v}=\int \frac{dx}{x}$

$\Rightarrow \ln |v^{3}+v|=\ln x+c$

$\Rightarrow \ln \left |\left (\frac{y}{x}\right )^{3}+\left (\frac{y}{x}\right )\right |=\ln x+C$

$↓~y(1)=1$

$\Rightarrow C=\ln 2$

$\therefore$ for $y(2)$

$\ln \left (\frac{y^{3}}{8}+\frac{y}{2}\right )=2\ln 2\Rightarrow \frac{y^{3}}{8}+\frac{y}{2}=4$

$\Rightarrow [y(2)]=2$

$\Rightarrow n=3$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text: Let $f$ be a twice differentiable function on $\mathrm{ℝ}$. If $f^{'}(0)=4$ and $f(x)+\int\limits _{0}^{x}(x-t)f^{'}(t)dt=\left (e^{2x}+e^{-2x}\right )\cos 2x+\frac{2}{a}x$, then $(2a+1)^{5}a^{2}$ is equal to $_______________$.

solution.body:

Here $f(0)=2...(ii)$

On differentiating equation (i) w.r.t. $x$ we get :

$\begin{array}{l} f^{'}(x)+\int\limits _{0}^{x}f^{'}(t)dt+xf^{'}(x)-xf^{'}(x) \\  \\ =2\left (e^{2x}-e^{-2x}\right )\cos 2x-2\left (e^{2x}+e^{-2x}\right )\sin 2x+\dfrac{2}{a} \\  \\ \Rightarrow f^{'}(x)+f(x)-f(0) \\  \\ =2\left (e^{2x}-e^{-2x}\right )\cos 2x-2\left (e^{2x}+e^{-2x}\right )\sin 2x+\dfrac{2}{a} \\  \\ \text{Replace}x\text{by}0\text{we get}: \\  \\ \Rightarrow 4=\dfrac{2}{a}\Rightarrow a=\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot  \\  \\ \therefore \quad (2a+1)^{5}\cdot a^{2}=2^{5}\cdot \dfrac{1}{2^{2}}=2^{3}=8 \end{array}$
